concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time such as O(n log n).

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of coefficients times powers of a variable, with addition, multiplication and evaluation.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a + bi with i² = −1, including roots of unity e^{2πi/q} and absolute value.

concepts.name: Turing machines and tapes
concepts.gloss: A finite-state machine with read/write heads moving one cell at a time on tapes; running time counts steps.

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of growth for the time to multiply two n-bit integers on a multitape Turing machine.

evidence.quote: proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model

concepts.name: Fixed finite-tape Turing machine model
concepts.gloss: One machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes; each step reads and writes one cell per tape and moves each head by at most one cell, and cost is the number of steps.

evidence.quote: A machine has one fixed finite alphabet and one fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes.
A step reads and writes at most one cell on each tape and moves each head by at most one cell.

concepts.name: Arrays, address fields and elementary scans
concepts.gloss: Arrays with a product address set are stored in lexicographic order on tape, with addresses implicit in position; fixed permutations of digits, digit moves, pointwise maps and cyclic row splits cost O(V) for V stored bits.

evidence.quote: An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.
takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes
The \emph{logical volume} $V$ is the number of stored data bits.

concepts.name: Controlled cyclic shifts and rational scalings
concepts.gloss: A linear-time tape operation that adds an offset computed from earlier control fields to a later target field modulo q^b, or multiplies it by a fixed unit, by splitting and re-merging blocks.

evidence.quote: Suppose a target field $y\in[Q]$ follows its control fields, each control used in an offset having $O(b)$ digits.
The next operations are linear because their target field follows their control fields.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication as digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing each integer as a polynomial in a power of two 2^b, the product's digit-coefficient list is the convolution of the two digit lists, followed by carry propagation.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.
Write the two inputs as polynomials in $2^b$, each with $q=\lceil n/b\rceil$ nonnegative digits.

concepts.name: Normalized DFT and cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The length-q discrete Fourier transform with 1/q normalization turns cyclic convolution into pointwise multiplication; its inverse uses the opposite sign of the exponent.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}
The normalized convolution rule is $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\mathbin{\cdot}

concepts.name: Multidimensional (tensor) Fourier transform
concepts.gloss: The tensor product of one-dimensional transforms along several axes; a transform on an array with axis lengths t_1,…,t_d is applied axis by axis.

evidence.quote: it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two
F_{\boldsymbol q}:=\bigotimes_iF_{q_i}

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map to prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism sending one cyclic convolution of length S = s_1⋯s_d (pairwise coprime) to a convolution on a product of d cyclic axes, implemented by triangular controlled cyclic shifts.

evidence.quote: the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves convolution
Agarwal and Cooley used the Chinese remainder theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's identity expressing a Fourier transform of coprime length s through a Fourier transform of a larger power-of-two length t, using Gaussian-weighted interpolation maps A and B₀.

evidence.quote: Gaussian resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a power-of-two tensor transform.
P_sF_s=2^{2\alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA

concepts.name: Fixed-point disk-grid arithmetic and contractions
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers stored as signed two's-complement integers scaled by 2^{-p} inside the unit disk; truncation Q_p toward zero costs error below √2·2^{-p}, and contractions never increase the sup norm so errors add up predictably.

evidence.quote: \mathbb D_p=\{2^{-p}(a+ib):a,b\in\mathbb Z,\ a^2+b^2\leq 2^{2p}\}
\|Q_p z-z\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}
Each normalized Fourier transform above is a contraction

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: the formal variable of the polynomials, subject to y^r = -1.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree below r with y^r = −1, where multiplication by a power of y is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: \mathcal R_r=\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)
Multiplication by $y^a$, for any integer $a$, permutes the coefficients and changes some signs; consequently it is an isometry for this norm.

concepts.name: Synthetic Fourier transform modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Synthetic Fourier transform modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: the formal variable of the polynomial ring, subject to y^r = -1.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: the number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: A Fourier transform over the ring modulo y^r + 1 whose roots of unity are powers of y, so twiddle multiplications are signed coefficient shifts; it satisfies a character-cancellation identity despite zero divisors.

evidence.quote: For a power of two $t$ dividing $2r$, define $\omega_t=y^{2r/t}$.
The ring has zero divisors, so we verify character cancellation directly instead of dividing by $\omega_t^j-1$.

concepts.name: Radix-2 butterfly layers and stored frequency order
concepts.gloss: Decimation in frequency: each level combines entries k and k+t/2 by the two-point butterfly H₀ and a twiddle monomial, leaving frequencies stored in bit-reversed order, which the opposite transform consumes directly.

evidence.quote: the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$ for
the entry $(F_t^-z)_j$ occupies slot $\operatorname{rev}_a(j)$

concepts.name: Twist from cyclic to negacyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k by ζ^k with ζ = e^{πi/r} is a ring isomorphism from the cyclic ring (x^r = 1) to the ring modulo y^r + 1, so its negative wrap yields the cyclic wrap after untwisting.

evidence.quote: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$
Untwisting therefore recovers the cyclic coefficient with the correct sign.

concepts.name: Established n log n multiplier as a subroutine
concepts.gloss: The Harvey–van der Hoeven O(N log N) integer multiplier is used as an ordinary subroutine on short inputs and does not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

evidence.quote: Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.
Harvey and van der Hoeven proved the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ bound

concepts.name: Signed Kronecker packing of polynomial products
concepts.gloss: Multiplying two polynomial records exactly by evaluating their integer-coefficient parts at a large power of two, multiplying the resulting integers with the established multiplier, and recovering signed coefficients by centered carries.

evidence.quote: Signed coefficient packing is a form of Kronecker substitution
Multiply the four pairs of absolute values using the established multiplier and restore each product's sign.

concepts.name: Bluestein's chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewrites a Fourier transform as a pointwise phase multiplication, a cyclic convolution with a chirp array, and another pointwise phase multiplication.

evidence.quote: Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform, including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution
a_{\boldsymbol j} =\exp\left(-\pi i\sum_{i=1}^d\frac{s_i j_i^2}{t_i}\right)

concepts.name: Resampling with the permutations left in the transform
concepts.gloss: The tensor form of Gaussian resampling in which the source and target coordinate permutations R and Q stay inside the transform identity, so they need not be executed as separate sorts.

evidence.quote: There are linear contractions $A:\mathbb C^s\to\mathbb C^t$ and $B_0:\mathbb C^t\to\mathbb C^s$ satisfying
RF_{\boldsymbol s} =2^\gamma\mathcal B_0QF_{\boldsymbol t}\mathcal A
We retain both permutations in the transform formula and compute that formula directly.

concepts.name: Chirp identity and source-permutation cancellation
concepts.gloss: A chirp-convolution formula for Q·F_t that leaves the target permutation unexecuted, together with the fact that the source permutation R cancels across the two forward transforms, the pointwise product and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: The chirp identity below performs the frequency change in $Q$ without applying $Q$ as a separate permutation of the array.
The second identity shows how the retained source permutation $R$ cancels when computing a convolution.

concepts.name: Three-element subset intersection gadget
concepts.gloss: Gather, scatter and side-injection updates indexed by three-element subsets of a 100-element set, whose coefficients depend on intersection size; side wires cancel the unwanted intersection-one (or intersection-zero/two) contributions.

evidence.quote: The construction uses three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted coefficients.
In the bit construction, scalars lie in $\mathbb F_2$, and $S,T$ are neighbors when $|S\cap T|=1$.

concepts.name: Linear network that exchanges two banks and restores scratch values
concepts.gloss: A fixed network of linear gates with three stages whose net effect is (X, Y) ↦ (−Y, X) on two banks, restoring every auxiliary scratch value whatever its initial contents.

evidence.quote: Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary value.
For arbitrary initial values of its auxiliary wires, a forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and leaves every other value unchanged.

concepts.name: Frames and the common-frame identity
concepts.gloss: An invertible operator D_v on each wire's address-indexed array at every network vertex; since gates are pointwise and linear they commute with a shared frame, so the whole network implements D_out S D_in⁻¹ and only edge changes D_v D_u⁻¹ cost anything.

evidence.quote: We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.
D_{\rm out}\,\mathsf S_\Omega\,D_{\rm in}^{-1}

concepts.name: Orthogonal complements and projections in a bilinear space
concepts.gloss: In a vector space with a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form, a subspace U has an orthogonal complement U⊥ and a projection P_U along it; the residual of nested subspaces has dimension equal to the difference of their dimensions.

evidence.quote: For a nondegenerate rational subspace $U\subset\mathcal F$, write $P_U$ for the projection onto $U$ along $U^\perp$.
the \emph{orthogonal residual} is the orthogonal complement of the smaller label inside the larger one

concepts.name: Nested subspace labels and the rank saving
concepts.gloss: Subspaces of an m-dimensional space attached to gates and terminals so adjacent labels are nested; edge dimension changes count the smaller operations needed, and their total s is strictly below W·m.

evidence.quote: The decisive property is that the total number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.
A label is a nondegenerate subspace of a fixed bilinear space.
Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

concepts.name: Lower-triangular rank factorization
concepts.gloss: Every rational square matrix of rank a factors as E₁ Π E₂ with E₁, E₂ invertible lower triangular and Π a partial permutation matrix with exactly a ones (a Bruhat factorization with coordinate order reversed).

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization
The required factorization is the Bruhat factorization for arbitrary matrices, with coordinate order reversed

concepts.name: Cost of a rational matrix shear
concepts.gloss: The address update (H, D) ↦ (H + AD, D) over Z/q^b is performed with exactly rank(A) interchanges of pairs of b-digit fields plus linear extra work, using triangular factors and controlled shifts.

evidence.quote: can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of pairs of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.
D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i,\qquad (H_i,D_j)\leftarrow(D_j,H_i),\qquad D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j.

concepts.name: Power-width chunk interchange in O(Ve^τ) time
concepts.title: Power-width chunk interchange in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: the number of data bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: the number of radix digits in each of the two interchanged chunks, a power of a fixed integer m.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: a fixed rational constant strictly between 0 and 1.

concepts.gloss: Recursively interchanges two chunks of e = m^k digits by running the bank-exchange network on W role streams of volume V/W, each edge costing rank-many smaller interchanges; since s/W < m^τ the cost per volume is O(e^τ).

evidence.quote: The chunks can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time, preserving every other address field, on a fixed number of finite-alphabet tapes.
F_0=O(1),\qquad F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1).
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Chunk interchange in O(Vu^τ) time
concepts.title: Chunk interchange in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: the number of data bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: the number of bits in each of the two interchanged address chunks.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: a fixed rational constant strictly below 1, namely 1 - 2^{-50}.

concepts.gloss: Interchanges two disjoint address chunks of u bits in any bit array in O(V u^τ) steps for a fixed τ < 1, by padding rows and splitting the width in base m into power-width pieces; intermediate steps are XOR combinations but the final effect is an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, where $V=PG B\,2^{2u}$
Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.
Although its final effect is an exact permutation, its intermediate steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data.

concepts.name: Two-point kernel C and the complex phase network
concepts.gloss: The Gaussian-dyadic two-point kernel C = H S H = aI + bX (a = (1+i)/2, b = (1−i)/2) satisfies H₀ = b S C S; the complex bank-exchange network with binary labels makes C^{⊗m} on every role from products of translation kernels, one per residual basis vector.

evidence.quote: C=H\mathsf SH=aI+bX
Its phase-frame difference $\mathcal C_V\mathcal C_U^{-1}$ is a product of one translation kernel $aI+bX_v$, or its inverse, per vector in an orthonormal basis of the edge residual.
H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_D C^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D

concepts.name: Packed XOR of selected bits across address chunks
concepts.gloss: A binary row addition y ← y ⊕ x on the selected bit of each of f chunks at once, done by a constant number of cyclic shifts of whole chunk ranges followed by deterministic repair of a small explicit set of bad addresses, using a third chunk as restored temporary space.

evidence.quote: We implement a binary row addition on corresponding selected bits in two address chunks.
The correction depends only on addresses, so the time bound is worst-case over all payloads.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer in O(Vd^λ') time
concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layer in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: the number of data bits stored in the array of records.

symbols.name: axis count
symbols.meaning: the number of equal-width address chunks (transform axes) whose selected bit is butterflied simultaneously.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: a fixed rational constant strictly below 1, namely 1 - 2^{-54}.

concepts.gloss: Applies the normalized butterfly H₀ to one bit position in each of d address chunks of polynomial records in one pass, exactly in Gaussian dyadics followed by a single truncation, in O(V d^λ') for a fixed λ' < 1 instead of d whole-array passes.

evidence.quote: coefficient order, and component format in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time
whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes
The procedure evaluates the entire layer exactly before this final truncation.

concepts.name: Layout and cost of the synthetic transform
concepts.gloss: A positional layout permutation puts the selected bits of all axes at a common offset in K-bit chunks so each transform round is one simultaneous layer; the forward transform keeps its output order for the pointwise product and the opposite transform.

evidence.quote: The procedure constructs an explicit positional layout permutation $L$ of record addresses, preserving their polynomial suffixes
The forward procedure may retain its output layout for a pointwise product and the following opposite procedure.

concepts.name: Convolution over the polynomial ring from the retained layout
concepts.gloss: Normalized convolution of arrays over the ring modulo y^r + 1: two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise ring products by signed packing, then the opposite transform consuming the same frequency order, with error O(M ℓ 2^{-p}).

evidence.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order.
\mathcal M_r(f,g)=\frac{f*g}{rM}=\frac{f*g}{T}

concepts.name: Source transform via resampling, chirp and ring convolution
concepts.gloss: The computed procedure for a source Fourier transform of prime lengths: Gaussian maps A, then a chirp transform evaluated by a twisted ring convolution, then B₀ and an exact power-of-two scale, with exact counterpart R F_s.

evidence.quote: write $\widetilde{\mathscr F}$ for the following procedure: apply the linewise approximation to $\mathcal A$, apply the computed chirp transform
\mathcal M_{\mathbb C}(f,g) :=D_-\iota^{-1} \mathcal M_r(\iota D_+f,\iota D_+g)

concepts.name: Choice of sizes, precision and prime axis lengths
concepts.gloss: Fixing b = ⌈log₂ n⌉, precision p = 6b, axis count d = ⌊b^ε⌋, padded size T ≈ n/b, record length r, power-of-two axis lengths t_i, and distinct odd prime lengths s_i just below t_i, so that Tp = Θ(n) and all hypotheses of the interfaces hold.

evidence.quote: b=\lceil\log_2n\rceil,\quad p=6b,\quad d=\lfloor b^\epsilon\rfloor
We may therefore choose distinct odd primes satisfying
\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50},\qquad \beta=\frac12,\qquad \delta=\frac1{16}

concepts.name: Exact recovery: scaling, rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Removing the known normalizations S and 2^{2b+4}, showing the recovered coefficient error is below 1/2 so rounding gives exact convolution coefficients, then propagating radix-2^b carries to the 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: proves that the recovered coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to obtain the exact binary product
Propagate radix-$2^b$ carries in increasing coefficient order.

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: Split into radix digits, map by Φ to prime axes, take two source transforms, multiply pointwise, apply the opposite-sign transform with the two scalings by S, round, undo Φ, and propagate carries to output the 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote: Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain source arrays $u,v$.
The two occurrences of $S$ in this algorithm undo different normalizations.

concepts.name: Cost accounting and the saving exponent κ
concepts.title: Cost accounting and the saving exponent $\kappa$

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: the fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the power of the logarithm is reduced below 1.

concepts.gloss: A table of costs divided by Tp, each at most p^{1−2κ} thanks to the slack in the chosen exponents (seven dominant margins, the smallest 2^{-181} = 2κ), giving O(n (log n)^{1−κ}) overall.

evidence.quote: Each of the seven displayed powers is at most $1-2\kappa$ by
Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.
This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Multiplying n-bit integers in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Multiplying $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: the number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: the fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the power of the logarithm is reduced below 1.

concepts.gloss: A single deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies two n-bit integers exactly in O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) worst-case time with κ = 2^{-182}, using fast address-chunk interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers to speed synthetic transforms inside a Gaussian-resampling multiplication.

evidence.quote: We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time
T_A(n)=O\!\left(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa}\right)

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and residues
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers taken modulo a positive integer q, where Z/qZ denotes the residue classes 0,...,q-1 with addition and multiplication reduced mod q.

concepts.name: Primes, divisibility, gcd and coprimality
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, two integers are coprime when their greatest common divisor is 1, and a residue is invertible modulo q exactly when it is coprime to q.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits with the leftmost bit most significant, padded on the left with zeros to a chosen length.

concepts.name: Bitwise XOR
concepts.gloss: The bit operation that outputs 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equivalently addition modulo 2, and it is its own inverse.

concepts.name: Logarithms, floors, ceilings and powers of two
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm, floor and ceiling functions, and the exponent rules used to size parameters such as b = ceil(log2 n).

concepts.name: Matrices, invertibility and rank
concepts.gloss: Matrices act as linear maps on vectors, are composed by multiplication, are invertible when a two-sided inverse exists, and have a rank equal to the dimension of their image.

concepts.name: Vector spaces, basis and dimension
concepts.gloss: The first-course linear-algebra notions of a vector space over a field such as the rationals or complex numbers, its subspaces, bases and dimension, and linear combinations of vectors.

concepts.name: Permutations and permutation matrices
concepts.gloss: A bijection of a finite index set to itself, which reorders entries of an array and is represented by a matrix with exactly one 1 in each row and column.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order and index tuples
concepts.gloss: Tuples of indices are ordered by comparing the first entry, then the second, and so on, which matches how a multidimensional array is laid out in a flat sequence.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and roots of unity as points on the unit circle
concepts.gloss: e^{i theta} = cos theta + i sin theta lies on the unit circle, so e^{2 pi i/q} is a q-th root of unity whose powers cycle with period q.

concepts.name: Geometric series and orthogonality of sums of roots of unity
aliases: sum of powers of a root of unity vanishes
concepts.gloss: The finite geometric series formula, and its consequence that the sum of all powers of a nontrivial q-th root of unity is zero while that of the trivial one is q.

concepts.name: Norms and the triangle inequality
concepts.gloss: A norm measures the size of a number or vector, obeys the triangle inequality, and is used to add up bounds on accumulated errors.

concepts.name: Rational numbers, dyadic rationals and exact arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Numbers of the form m/2^k with integer m, closed under addition and multiplication, and the idea that exact arithmetic on them is separate from rounding or truncating a real number.

concepts.name: Algebraic structures: groups, rings and isomorphisms
concepts.gloss: The basic definitions from a discrete-mathematics course of a set with operations satisfying axioms, and of a structure-preserving bijection between two such sets.

concepts.name: Discrete-math proof techniques
concepts.gloss: Proof by induction, recursive definitions and recurrences, and elementary counting, as used to bound the cost of a recursive procedure.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and divide-and-conquer multiplication
concepts.gloss: The standard O(n^2) digit-by-digit method for multiplying integers with carries, and the idea that splitting numbers into pieces can beat it.

concepts.name: Multitape machine cost model and linear-time scans
concepts.gloss: Time on a Turing machine counts head steps, so reading, copying or comparing a tape of N cells in order costs O(N), while random access to arbitrary cells costs more.

concepts.name: Complex polynomial evaluation and interpolation
concepts.gloss: A polynomial of degree below r is determined by its r coefficients or by its values at r distinct points, and these two representations are interchangeable.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function exp(-x^2), which decays rapidly away from zero and is used here as a smooth weight whose tails can be dropped with small error.

concepts.name: Convolution as polynomial multiplication
concepts.gloss: The convolution of two sequences has k-th entry equal to the sum of the products of entries whose indices add to k, which is exactly the coefficient list of the product of the corresponding polynomials.

concepts.name: Quantifiers, sets and basic asymptotic notation beyond big-O
concepts.gloss: The notation Theta and Omega for tight and lower bounds, little-o for strictly smaller growth, and the distinction between worst-case upper bounds and lower bounds on an algorithm's running time.

background.summary: The reader is an undergraduate computer scientist: fluent in asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (sets, functions, modular arithmetic, primes and gcd, permutations, induction and recursion), first-course linear algebra (matrices, invertibility, rank, basis, dimension, linear maps over the rationals and the complex numbers), complex arithmetic with Euler's formula, and the basic Turing machine model with tapes and step counting. They have seen binary representation, bit operations such as XOR, and perhaps the idea of multiplying integers by divide and conquer, but have not been taught the discrete Fourier transform, the FFT, polynomial transforms, Schönhage–Strassen, abstract ring theory beyond the basic definition, tensor products, or numerical error analysis, and these are what the wiki must explain.
